evidence.claim: Southern Pines lies in the Sandhills, where longleaf pines once supplied timber, ships’ masts and resin for naval stores.
evidence.quote: Merchants cut the forests for timber and cultivated choice stands for use as masts for the Royal Navy ships. Merchants also harvested resin from the longleaf pines for the naval stores industry.

evidence.quote: As a result of logging and naval stores operations, most of the virgin growth of longleaf pines had disappeared from the Sandhills by 1900.

flags: Partial overview: all three NCDOT cache files contain identical guidebook text truncated during the Historic Flat Rock chapter. Page fragments in their URLs do not retrieve pages 172–174. East Connecticut Avenue appears only in the contents and statewide index.

Consequently cache cannot verify avenue length, curves, terrain, start point, direction, endpoint, horse farms, estates along the road, route-specific designation rationale, or construction and designation history. Intro is deliberately short and gives regional context rather than unsupported end-to-end directions.

Dropped current claims: three-block offset from Broad Street, southeast course, under-three-mile length, soft curves and rolling ground, roadside estates and horse farms, North Fort Bragg Road endpoint and base entrance, deep coarse sand between Piedmont and coastal plain, John T. Patrick attribution, and failure of the health-resort plan.

Retained Southern Pines and Weymouth Woods metadata exactly. New James Boyd House uses its cached coordinates; placed between town and preserve using supplied strip order and coordinates. Cache does not establish direct access from the avenue.

Oldest-known longleaf claim is supported by the secondary cache but omitted because record status is time-sensitive and no dated park source is cached. No promise of interior access at the Boyd house or current preserve hours is made.
Current story has no motifs; story array is empty and retained moment motifs remain absent.
James Boyd House is short because its dedicated cache provides only a compact architectural and reuse history.
The 1898 exclusion of African Americans is documented only in the cached town article; no underlying local record or community history is included in the cache.
